summary: Revise at 6.6, up from 6.0 (Caiman is 7, the ship bar 7.5). Every gate is now green. The template is 2,752,225 bytes, under the declared painted class's 3 MB. The ray release is recorded as not applying under Logan's lost-wax rule, as Manticora's shipped review also treats it. The export count matching the draft count is explained by the stock's fixed stored surface. Round 2 fixed four of round 1's art items. The tail now ends in a tip on the face. The ground cells have mostly clean rims. The palm lamellae are crescents with a centre chevron. A tubercle row now runs down each side face. The read still holds at 300 px: a jeweller says 'gecko'. The craft is still clip-art, not a dark-mythology cast. The head is a smooth, featureless blob, with no brow, jaw, nostrils or skull planes. The eyes are still balls stuck on the head's corners. The lower one sits at the jaw like a knuckle, and both carry torn, notched pupil cuts (stones.png). The torso is still a smooth sausage carrying the same ringed, rivet-like domes; punch item 6 was not done. The shoulder crowns between the face and the tubercle rows are large bare polished areas, about 8 x 6 mm a side. The tubercle 'rows' are one single file of beads, which reads as beaded trim. Seen side-on, the lamellae read as sawtooth gear teeth with hard blocky drops (side.png, reverse.png). The face border still shows a streaky, smeared margin band at the upper right (hero.png). Round 3 is the last. To reach 7.5 it must model the head and eyes, rebuild the spots, and fill the shoulders.
strengths: The animal still reads at 300 px with no caption. The splayed limbs with disc-toed five-toe fans, seen from above, make the gecko emblem (face-300.png, hero-300.png).
The tail is finished. It sweeps down from the hip in an S and ends in a tapered tip inside the face. The smeared stub at the face's edge is gone (face.png).
The pebbled ground is much cleaner. Most cells now have smooth, closed rims, and a calm halo separates the figure from the ground (stones.png).
The palm lamellae now read as curved scansor plates rather than a radiator: crescent leading edges, a visible grade, and the split chevron at 270° (palm.png).
The theme now leaves the face. A tubercle row runs down each side face to the lamellae (side.png, shoulder.png).

All the gates are green, including the template gate that failed in round 1. The wall census is clean under the lead's interim rule: 0 real wall zones, 0 unresolved, and one 0.004 mm zone listed as an artifact.
The factory 017 hard wall-to-face angle is kept round the whole face (bare-vs-finished.png).

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: It is better than round 1, but still not continuous. A single bead row on each side face links the face to the lamellae. The shoulder crowns under both ends of the face, and the upper flanks, are large bare polished areas (shoulder.png, hero.png, reverse.png show about 8 x 6 mm a side). The planned granules on the shoulder crown are still missing.

checklist.item: Hide reads as this specific animal at 300 px
checklist.reason: The posture and toe pads say 'gecko'. The hide does not say 'tokay'. The body carries ringed button domes, a polka-dot cartoon rather than a tokay's tubercle spotting. The ground is generic pebbling, and the shank's bead file is generic beading.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true, crisp outlines
checklist.reason: The eye pupils are still torn, notched cuts. The lower eye shows a ragged rectangular notch (stones.png). The face margin band shows streaky, smeared facets at the upper right (hero.png, stones.png top edge). The lamella arcs are broken into dashes in palm.png. The limbs, toes and tail have clean outlines.

checklist.item: Stones sit in made settings and are visible
checklist.reason: N/A. No stone: stones.json is empty, and reported 0 equals previewed 0.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms sculpted
checklist.reason: The head and torso are unmodelled smooth blobs, with no brow, jaw, nostrils, shoulder or hip masses, or spine. The spots are identical domes in grooved rings, like rivets. The eyes are spheres. The side-on lamellae are blocky sawtooth plates with vertical drops, like gear teeth (side.png, reverse.png).

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: The 017 edge is crisp all round (bare-vs-finished.png, face.png).

checklist.item: Silhouette distinct from other Cataphracta rings and the Reptilia tiles
checklist.reason: It is still the 017 tonneau on a tapering shank. The flat face with its low relief differs from Varanus's ridged roof face, but the outline is the same stock: nothing breaks the profile at the corners or the shoulders. Round 1's item 9 was not done.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: The large form (the figure) and the small form (the pebbling) are present. The medium tier is weak: the spots are uniform, and the head has no sub-forms. Density off the face is far below Caiman, which is worked on every surface. Here the bare shoulders and the smooth body dominate the hero.

punch_list.zone: Tokay head and eyes (right end of the face, the stored 'Tokay' and 'Eyes' parts)
punch_list.change: Sculpt the head. Broaden the rear of the skull to about 1.4x the neck width, with a raised brow ridge over each eye (0.2-0.3 mm proud). Cut a shallow jaw line from the snout tip to below each eye, and add two nostril dots at the snout. Re-seat both eyes symmetrically on the head's rear-upper corners, each half sunk into the skull and breaking the side outline by about 0.4 mm. Today the lower eye sits at the jaw like a knuckle. Replace the torn pupil cuts with a clean vertical groove (0.25 mm wide, 0.12 mm deep, smooth ends), and give each eye a smooth 0.2 mm lid rim.
punch_list.acceptance: In stones.png both eyes sit mirror-symmetric on the head's outline, with unbroken pupil grooves and lid rims and no notches. Brow, jaw and nostrils are visible. In face-300.png the head reads as a broad, big-eyed gecko head, not a smooth bulb.

punch_list.zone: Tokay torso spots and body form (face centre)
punch_list.change: This is round 1's item 6, not done. Remove the groove ring around every spot. Use 12-16 low, flat-topped, irregular spots, 0.8-1.6 mm across and 0.15-0.25 mm proud, varied in size and shape, in two loose dorsal rows plus scattered flank spots. Model the shoulder and hip swells over the limb roots (0.2-0.3 mm), a faint spine ridge, and a waist taper.
punch_list.acceptance: In face.png and stones.png no spot has a ring groove or reads as a rivet or button. The torso shows distinct shoulder and hip masses and a spine line, and in face-300.png the spots still read.

punch_list.zone: Shoulder crowns and upper flanks (about 20-70° and 110-160°, from the face edge to the start of the tubercle row)
punch_list.change: Fill the bare shoulders with the planned crown granules. Grade them from the face's cell size (0.6-1.0 mm) at the face edge to about half that by 200°/340°, at 0.15-0.2 mm height. Start the tubercle rows at the face's wall instead of about 6 mm below it.
punch_list.acceptance: In hero.png, shoulder.png and reverse.png no polished area larger than about 3 x 3 mm remains outside the bore, and the texture runs unbroken from the face's edge to the lamellae.

punch_list.zone: Side faces, the tubercle rows (both sides, about 20-250° and 290-160°)
punch_list.change: Turn the single file of beads into tokay tubercle rows. Use 2-3 staggered rows of enlarged, slightly conical tubercles (0.5-0.8 mm across, 0.3-0.4 mm high) on the helix shear, with fine granules between them, as the section specifies.
punch_list.acceptance: In side.png and shoulder.png the side faces show staggered, spiralling rows of tubercles over a granular ground, not one line of beads.

punch_list.change: Soften the lamella drops. Round each trailing drop with a 0.15-0.2 mm radius, and lower the drop to about 0.3 mm so the plates read as overlapping pads, not sawteeth. Close the broken arcs so each crescent is one continuous edge across the band.
punch_list.acceptance: In side.png and reverse.png the palm profile reads as a soft scalloped edge, not gear teeth. In palm.png every crescent is unbroken from wall to wall.

punch_list.zone: Face margin band (the strip between the ground and the wall-to-face edge, worst at the upper right)
punch_list.change: Remove the streaky, smeared facets in the margin. Make the ground's outer step a clean, uniform land about 0.5 mm wide, with a single crisp step down to the polished border.
punch_list.acceptance: In hero.png and stones.png the margin band is smooth polish, with no streaks or starburst facets along any edge.

punch_list.zone: Silhouette at the face corners or a shoulder
punch_list.change: Break the 017 outline once. For example, let the forward toe fans lap over the face edge onto the wall by 1.0-1.5 mm, or carry the tail tip over the left shoulder. Keep the factory's wall-to-face angle elsewhere.
punch_list.acceptance: Set beside the Varanus tile at the same angle, the hero-300 outline differs visibly at a face corner or a shoulder.
